gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many iPhone 17-generation charges a 10,000 mAh bank actually delivers: 10,000 mAh × 0.58 measured efficiency = 5,800 mAh, which is 1.57 charges of an iPhone 17 (3,692 mAh), 1.36 of a 17 Pro, 1.14 of a 17 Pro Max and 1.84 of an iPhone Air.
standout_why: Compared against Engadget (measured 58% delivered and 1.86 / 1.64 charges, but only on an iPhone 15), oscarmini (rule of thumb 0.65 × capacity on a generic 5,000 mAh phone, 1.3 charges), powerbank-online (generic 4,000 mAh phone, 1.6 charges) and knowledgelib (generic 65–70% usable, no phone named). None applies a measured efficiency to Apple's own iPhone 17 battery figures, none gives mAh per ounce or dollars per 1,000 mAh, and none notes that Anker's own support page claims 'at least 2 to 3' phone charges from the Nano 10K while a measured-efficiency derivation gives about 1.6 on an iPhone 17. TechRadar and WSJ could not be read (truncated / blocked).
decides: It confirms a 10,000 mAh bank is the right size for a phone (1.1–1.8 full charges across the iPhone 17 line, so a 5,000 mAh bank would fall short of one full Pro Max charge) and shows all four 10K candidates deliver the same energy, so the pick turns on weight and price per capacity: the INIU Carry Slim 45W carries about 25% more mAh per ounce than the Anker Nano 10K 45W (1,532 vs 1,225 mAh/oz) at under half the dollars per 1,000 mAh ($2.50 vs $6.00). The Anker Nano's 30 W input also sets a refill floor of about 1.2 hours, the fastest of the group on paper.

findings.label: Full charges per 10,000 mAh bank, derived
findings.value: iPhone 17 1.57; iPhone Air 1.84; 17 Pro 1.36; 17 Pro Max 1.14
findings.source_title: The best power banks and portable chargers for every device in 2026 - Engadget
findings.note: 5,800 mAh delivered (Engadget) ÷ phone battery (Notebookcheck/Apple): 5,800 ÷ 3,692 = 1.57; ÷ 3,149 = 1.84; ÷ 4,252 = 1.36; ÷ 5,088 = 1.14. Applies equally to all four 10,000 mAh candidates; wireless use of the Baseus AM52 would deliver less.
